document_summary: This procedure outlines how field technicians collect, record, and escalate drinking water quality samples in municipal operations.

edits.rationale: Title is clear and accurate; no changes needed.

edits.revised: Purpose: This procedure explains how field teams collect and record drinking water samples so that results are reliable and traceable to the correct site.
edits.rationale: Sentence is grammatically correct and clear.

edits.revised: Scope: It applies to routine samples collected from reservoirs, treatment outlets, and public taps. The procedure does not cover emergency chemical spills or laboratory instrument calibration.
edits.rationale: Clear and consistent with the rest of the document.

edits.revised: Responsibilities: The team leader checks that each technician has PBT, clean sample bottles, and a calibrated meter. Technicians are responsible for completing the Chain of Custody Form QMS-07 and reporting unsafe conditions.
edits.rationale: Responsibilities are clearly stated; no changes needed.

edits.revised: Procedure: Before collecting a sample, allow the tap to run for 2 minutes. Rinse the probe with clean water, but do not rinse a sterile microbiological bottle. Record pH and turbidity in NTU at the site. Samples must be placed in a cooler between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius.
edits.rationale: Instructions are clear and technically accurate.

edits.revised: Data recording: Write the site code, date, time, and sampler initials on both the bottle and QMS-07. Corrections must be made with a single line through the error; correction fluid is not allowed. The reason for any missing reading must be stated.
edits.rationale: Clear and consistent with standard data recording practices.

edits.revised: Escalation: If pH is below 6.5 or above 9.5, or turbidity is higher than 1 NTU, phone the team leader immediately. Do not tell the community that the water is safe or unsafe until the authorised official has reviewed the result.
edits.rationale: Clear and unambiguous; no changes needed.

translations.translated: Maikaelelo: Mokgwa o o tlhalosa gore ditlhopha tsa kwa ntle di kgobokanya le go kwala disampole tsa metsi a go nwa jang gore dipholo di nne tse di tshephegang le tse di ka latelwang kwa lefelong le le siameng.

translations.translated: Kakaretso: O dira ka disampole tsa tlwaelo tse di tserweng mo matamong, mo mafelong a go alafa metsi, le mo dipompong tsa setšhaba. Mokgwa o ga o akaretse tshetleho ya dikhemikale tsa tshoganetso kgotsa go lekanyetsa didirisiwa tsa kwa laboratoring.

translations.translated: Maikarabelo: Moeteledipele wa setlhopha o tlhatlhoba gore motekheniki mongwe le mongwe o na le PBT, dibotlelana tsa disampole tse di phepa, le selekanyetsi se se lekanyeditsweng. Batekheniki ba na le maikarabelo a go tlatsa Foromo ya QMS-07 ya Chain of Custody le go bega maemo a a sa bolokehang.

translations.translated: Mokgwa: Pele o tsaya sampole, letla pompo e elele ka metsotso e 2. Tlhatswa probe ka metsi a a phepa, mme o se ka wa tlhatswa botlhelo jo bo sa bolaeng jwa microbiological. Kwala pH le turbidity ka NTU kwa lefelong. Disampole di tshwanetse go bewa mo setsidifatsing magareng ga 2 le 8 degrees Celsius.

translations.translated: Go kwala datha: Kwala khoutu ya lefelo, letlha, nako, le ditšhupiso tsa motlhatlheledi mo botlhelong le mo QMS-07. Diphoso di tshwanetse go suthisiwa ka mola o le mongwe go ralala phoso; ga go letlelelwe go dirisa setlhotlho sa go phimola. Lebaka la go tlhoka go bala lepe le tshwanetse go tlhalosiwa.
